A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and rendered figures support reliable comparison despite added sections and relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations on BoolQ, ALFWorld, HotPotQA, and HumanEval, together with interpretability analyses and mitigation experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds DeepSeek evaluations, comparisons across correction prompts, recovery rates, and additional quantitative analyses.

M1.justification: Tuned-lens probing, PACT, question repeating, and the few-sample SFT procedure are retained. The additional correction prompts are evaluated alternatives, rather than revisions to the proposed interpretation or mitigation methods.

E1.justification: The four datasets and tasks remain unchanged. Appendix C adds BoolQ scenarios supplying alternative reference answers, with and without generated feedback. These extend the information supplied to the model beyond the earlier confirmation and denial probes.

E2.justification: V2 expands the performance and mitigation comparisons to denial, reference-answer, feedback-and-refinement, and reference-assisted feedback prompts (Tables 14–15 and 18–19). V1 already compared denial with confirmation in internal-confidence probing, but did not include this broader comparator set in the accuracy and mitigation comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 adds a systematic comparison across five prompting protocols, including explicit feedback generation for BoolQ, and evaluates DeepSeek R1/V3. It also introduces wrong-to-correct rates and prompt/output-length measurements. The original dataset sample counts remain unchanged; removing the temperature disclosure does not establish an actual temperature change.

E4.justification: New Appendix C and Section G.2 test whether failures and mitigation effectiveness persist across correction prompts. Table 3 adds length-based analyses of cognitive overload and perfectionism. Its overthinking counts, the case-study logs, and the SFT sample-size analysis already appeared in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional descriptive averages and transition percentages do not introduce an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Matched original table entries remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results. Table 1 reports DeepSeek R1/V3 accuracies of 78.1%/69.0%; Tables 12–15 and 18–19 add recovery and multi-prompt outcomes. Table 18 shows question repeating can hurt GPT-4o under Prompt4, reducing accuracy from 81.9% to 81.4%. Figure 2 adds DeepSeek curves and removes o1-mini.

T1.justification: The tuned-lens expression, PACT definitions, multi-token log-probability expression, and Jensen–Shannon aggregation in Equations 1–6 are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation appears.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain explaining self-correction failures through answer wavering, prompt bias, and human-like cognitive bias, and mitigating them through question repeating and SFT. The added model and prompt evaluations support these retained claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges successful self-corrections and qualifies question repeating as effective only in most tested prompt conditions. Its new limitations discussion dates the experiments before February 15, 2025 and reports informal observations of fewer failures in newer GPT-4o, limiting applicability to updated models.

D1.justification: V2 supplies full templates for the additional prompting protocols and an experimental cutoff date. It removes v1's explicit temperature-zero statement and prose specifying balanced Yes/No SFT labels, although the displayed training examples remain unchanged. The code-access address is retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Paul et al. (2023), Welleck et al. (2022), and Wu et al. (2024), discussing their correction approaches as outside scope. It removes Schramowski et al. (2022) and Sweller (1988). The main related-work organization and contribution positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained, with localized tightening and author/affiliation edits. V2 adds Limitations, Ethics Statement, Acknowledgement, two appendix sections, and a mitigation subsection, while renumbering the existing appendices.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the quantitative displays with Table 3, transition-rate Tables 12–13, and multi-prompt comparison Tables 14–15 and 18–19. Figure 1 adds DeepSeek and Figure 2 changes curves and legends. Existing appendix figures are largely retained and relocated; Figure 20 also receives a terminology edit.

improvement.justification: The added prompt comparisons and successful-correction rates make the evidence more informative and balanced, including revealing limits of question repeating. The timestamp caveat clarifies applicability. These gains outweigh the loss of temperature disclosure, but remain limited: the added length associations do not establish the proposed causal mechanisms, and several added prompt conditions supply external cues.
